name: La Loge
funding: Flemish Government, French Community, VGC, Ixelles, COCOF, Brussels-Capital Region and the National Lottery, plus First Sight members.
watch: Non-profit space in a former Masonic temple in Ixelles. It programmes contemporary art, architectural theory and commissions.
records_note: Names its public funders and its board, undated, but posts no annual report or accounts.

name: LACE (Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions)
funding: California Arts Council, Andy Warhol Foundation, National Endowment for the Arts, Mike Kelley Foundation. 501(c)(3) public non-profit returns.
watch: Founded in 1978 by artists; the longest-running non-profit artist-run space in Los Angeles. Known for experimental performance, social justice programmes and video archives.

name: Lalit Kala Akademi
funding: Autonomous body funded by the Union Ministry of Culture, founded in 1954. It runs the National Exhibition, the Triennale-India and seven regional centres.
watch: The government took over its management in April 2015, citing irregularities. A 2017 Delhi High Court petition claimed misappropriation of funds.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2012-13 to 2018-19 and names its Executive Board; no audited accounts or funder list found.

name: Laongo Granite Sculpture Symposium
funding: Burkina Faso's culture ministry organises it and pays professional artists' fees, flights and stay, per its 2024 call for applications. No other funder is named.
watch: Founded 1989 by Siriki Ky, 35 km from Ouagadougou. The 15th edition runs 2 to 23 November 2026 under President Traoré's patronage.
records_note: Run by the culture ministry with no site of its own; the ministry site is down, so reports, accounts and board could not be checked.

name: Le Consortium
funding: Ministry of Culture and DRAC, City of Dijon, Région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, Côte-d'Or council. Private partners: DVF, Groupe Roger Martin, art foundations, Friends of Le Consortium.
watch: Artist-led contemporary art center (Centre d'art contemporain d'intérêt national).
records_note: Names its public funders, Friends and main private supporters, and lists the association's three-person executive board; no annual reports or accounts are posted.

name: Lenbachhaus
funding: City of Munich gallery. On 18 September 2025 the council accepted gifts from Beisheim Stiftung, Pro Helvetia, Art Mentor Foundation Lucerne and Herbert Schuchardt-Stiftung.
watch: Operated by the City of Munich as a municipal cultural institution.
records_note: A Munich city gallery with no report or board of its own; the city posts consolidated accounts, and the gallery names six foundations, undated.

name: Leopold Museum
funding: Federal ministry subsidy. Sponsors: Siwacht, Post, PORR, Arbeiterkammer Wien, Dorotheum, im Kinsky; partner Wiener Städtische (insurer).
watch: Private foundation set up with state money in 1994 to house Rudolf Leopold's Schiele collection. Its early 20th-century Austrian works face provenance scrutiny under the federal Art Restitution Act.
records_note: Names two partners in text and shows the rest as logos; it posts no annual report, accounts or foundation board.

name: Lismore Castle Arts
funding: Not-for-profit initiative founded 2005. Exhibitions are funded by the Arts Council and the Waterford City & County Council Arts Grant; an older page also lists the Henry Moore Foundation.
watch: Non-profit contemporary exhibition space in County Waterford.
records_note: No annual report, accounts or board; the about page credits the Arts Council and the Waterford City and County Council arts grant, undated.

name: Long Museum
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, donor list or board found; archived pages name only the founders Liu Yiqian and Wang Wei.

name: Lugar a Dudas
funding: Non-profit cultural foundation supported by Prince Claus Fund, DOEN Foundation, artist philanthropy from Oscar Muñoz, and international grants.

name: Lusaka Contemporary Art Centre (LuCAC)
funding: Founder Victor Mutelekesha's household paid for the building. Pro Helvetia paid for shelving; OCA, a Norwegian arts body, part-financed the 2023 opening show; the late artist Jan Groth donated.
watch: Opened 6 January 2023 in New Chamba Valley with a gallery, library and artist residency; first show Prospice, Kwacha!
records_note: Names its eleven-member advisory board; publishes no annual reports, accounts or funder list.

name: MACAAL
funding: Fondation Alliances, set up in 2009 by Othman Lazraq, funds it. The Lazraq family runs the listed property developer Alliances. No other funder is named.
watch: Museum of African Contemporary Art Al Maaden in Marrakech.
records_note: MACAAL's site covers exhibitions, mission and visits, and links its founder, Fondation Alliances, but posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board.
